retell: British politicians say their government relies so much on American online-storage companies that the US could switch off British services, though ministers say the data stays in Britain.
A French electrical company is buying a Boston factory-software company for 22.6 billion dollars, regulators still have to agree, and the French company's shares dropped 8 percent.
Two chip companies, Qualcomm from the US and Huawei from China, agreed to share inventions and this time Qualcomm pays Huawei, which is a first.
A top Japanese central banker thinks AI will make the economy so busy that borrowing money may stay more expensive than people expect, but nothing is decided.
Hackers pretended to work at a company called Anthropic and tricked American experts into opening emails with a virus, and a security company thinks China is behind it.
problem: 'Anthropic' is never introduced; a stranger does not know what it is or why posing as its employee would get experts to open the emails.
fix_headline: Hackers posed as staff of AI firm Anthropic to slip malware to US AI policy experts.
fix_body: Security firm Proofpoint says a China-linked group invited experts to a made-up advisory committee. Later emails carried malware aimed at cloud accounts; the China link is Proofpoint's own view.

retell: A big bank says even though almost nobody wants a giant computer building near their home, the number of them in America will still grow almost as fast as it predicted.
problem: 'nudged its estimates up' does not say estimates of what; 'data center' is never explained, so a stranger cannot tell what is being opposed or forecast.
fix_body: Its data center growth estimate rose for next year and fell for the year after. Power use by these huge computer halls should still grow 38 percent yearly; few Americans want one nearby.

retell: The world's biggest chip factory company wants to charge up to 6 percent more for its best chips next year because so many people want them, but it has not confirmed this.
Germany is buying tens of thousands of drones, built in Ukraine by a Munich company, whose job is to hunt down Russian attack drones.
A start-up backed by Nvidia is said to be about to release a powerful American AI model that anyone can download and change, nearly as good as China's best.
Korean scientists found that AI tools predicting whether drugs are safe got tested on molecules almost identical to the ones they learned from, so they looked smarter than they are.
The boss of OpenAI says we should put up with some damage from AI to get its benefits, but he still says disasters like losing control of AI are a different matter.
problem: 'rejects catastrophic risks' is unclear: it could mean he dismisses them or that he refuses to accept them; 'rival Anthropic' is not introduced as an AI company.
fix_body: The OpenAI chief told Politico he and rival AI firm Anthropic differ widely on rules. He still draws the line at catastrophic risks such as losing control of AI; no rule has changed.

retell: Stanford used 37,000 AI programs to read old medicine tests and found that drugs aimed at genes used by only a few kinds of cells got further 40 percent more often, though that is just a pattern.
problem: 'AI agents' is jargon; 'advanced 40 percent more often' does not say advanced where (through the trials), so the result reads as a fragment.
fix_headline: Stanford researchers set 37,000 AI helpers to read old drug trials for success clues.
fix_body: Drugs for genes active in few cell types advanced in trials 40 percent more often. This is a pattern in past records, not proof; the AI helpers ran no lab experiments.

retell: McDonald's uses AI to suggest prices at almost all its US restaurants, nearby stores ended up charging very different prices for a Big Mac, and some owners feel they have to go along.
People paid to teach AI how to do their own jobs believe their creativity keeps them safe, while a famous economist warns unemployment could triple in ten years at worst.
A Florida pizza shop got famous online by promising it will never use AI, and the owner has made pizza by hand since 1991.
IBM says its new quantum computer chip solved in 19 seconds a problem a normal supercomputer would need a hundred years for.
The former boss of GitHub started a new place for programmers to store their code that runs on many computers instead of one company's servers.
problem: 'GitHub' and 'code-hosting' are never explained, so a stranger does not know what the company does or what was launched.
fix_headline: The ex-boss of code-storage site GitHub launched a rival spread across many machines.

retell: An expert says twelve gun turrets aimed by AI now protect Kyiv from Russian drones.
Investors want ways to protect their savings because AI companies now make up such a big slice of the stock market.
Investors keep pouring money into AI companies even though borrowing is the most expensive it has been in 24 years, so keep an eye on US bond rates.
problem: 'the AI rally leans on them' has an unclear 'them' (rates? bonds?) and does not say why rates above 5 percent matter; 'Anthropic' is not introduced.
fix_body: Schneider buys PTC for $22.6 billion; AI firm Anthropic reportedly plans a November share sale. Watch US bond rates above 5 percent: AI stocks need cheap loans.
